progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: First video of this series: a gamete carries one set of chromosomes and one set plus one set makes the full two sets in the zygote. The animals video: mammals fertilise internally and invest in a few young. Year 11: cells, enzymes, mitochondria and diffusion as movement from more to less. No hormone and no menstrual cycle is assumed.
progression.startsWith: A home pregnancy test that detects a chemical the embryo makes, and the question of what has to happen after a sperm joins an egg.
progression.stopsAfter: Tracing a human pregnancy from fertilisation in the oviduct, through cleavage and the blastocyst, to implantation in a lining prepared by progesterone from the corpus luteum; explaining why the embryo's hCG is needed; stating that the placenta takes over progesterone over the first two to three months after fertilisation; describing placental exchange without blood mixing; separating embryo from fetus; and not confusing hCG (acts on the corpus luteum) with progesterone (acts on the lining).
progression.nextLesson: B3a part 2: how birth starts and why labour speeds up (oxytocin, the cervix, positive feedback, and milk).

teaching.task: Trace how a pregnancy is established and kept going, and explain why a tiny embryo needs to send a hormone message.
teaching.causalExplanation: Fertilisation in the oviduct makes a zygote that divides without growing into a blastocyst, which implants in a lining that the corpus luteum's progesterone keeps thick. With no pregnancy the corpus luteum breaks down about two weeks after the egg is released, progesterone falls and the lining is shed, so the embryo's outer cells make hCG, which keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone. Over the first two to three months the placenta takes over, and it passes oxygen and nutrients to the baby and wastes back across thin membranes without the bloods mixing.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on a pregnancy test that detects the embryo's message, builds a numbered rail (meet, divide, attach, signal, hand over), draws one progesterone graph a stage at a time across the lining, hCG and hand-over scenes, and tests the model with an IVF-style, a timing and a misconception question.
teaching.openingDecision: A sperm has just joined an egg. What has to happen next before there is a pregnancy, and why would a tiny embryo need to send a message?
teaching.understandingCheck: Predict what happens when a blastocyst reaches a uterus with no progesterone, what happens if the corpus luteum stops three weeks versus five months after fertilisation while the embryo makes hCG, and correct a student who says the mother's blood flows into the fetus's blood.
teaching.curriculumScope: Analyse the features of fertilisation, implantation and hormonal control of pregnancy in a scoped human mammalian model (Module 5). Feedback loops, birth, lactation, oestrogen and oxytocin are in part 2; contraception, haploid and diploid and meiosis are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, painted reproductive tract, cleavage, blastocyst, implantation and fetus-and-placenta plates with coded gamete close-ups, a progesterone graph, hormone particles, an organ chain, a numbered rail and a placental exchange close-up. Colour key: amber progesterone, teal hCG and embryo tissue, yellow outline corpus luteum, rose mother's blood, purple baby's blood.
design.transitionPlan: The test stick hooks onto the embryo; the tract plate gains labels and a camera push; a lens pushes into the gametes and the zygote; the cleavage plates crossfade inside a fixed outline while a dot travels the oviduct; the camera pushes to the uterus wall and the lining; implantation plates crossfade; the graph enlarges and slides to the rail; the placenta plate and exchange close-up follow; the attempt board removes the rail and it returns in the memory scene; scene crossfade with settle.
